newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on commercial stopping.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on commercial stopping.

text.p: Strong commercial stopping of the deliveries posted Wednesday against the September contract and signals the wheat market was oversold boosted CBOT wheat futures to a higher close, traders said.
"Wheat already was beat up and the funds were short plus Continental stopped the wheat," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Continental Grain Wednesday stopped all of the 700,000 bushels posted for delivery on the September contract.
Nearby September, set to expire at 1201 CDT Thursday, was strong because of the aggressive commercial demand.
Also traders were getting out of that contract before the expiration day. Traders said a high open interest figure in September wheat spelled out a potential for volatility in the September contract.
Questions about whether or not a sale of French wheat to Egypt will be completed may have buoyed the market.
But gains in wheat were limited by increased competition for export business from overseas growers along with increased supplies of wheat worldwide, the traders said.
Wheat closed 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher to two lower, with September up 9-1/2 at $4.32-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, up from 11,994 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, LFG Futures bought 400 December $4.30 puts and sold 400 December $4.00 puts at 16-1/2 cents, Griffin Trading bought 300 December $3.80 puts at 2-1/4 cents and Smith Barney bought 300 December $3.80 puts at 2-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, up from 4,447 Wednesday.
